title: Bounded monadic categorical argument candidate validation
independentExamples: A sufficient-premise task where an existential negative fact and a renamed class inclusion entail a renamed conclusion.
A necessary-conclusion task where an existential witness propagates through a renamed inclusion and produces a different categorical conclusion.
preconditions: Every premise, conclusion when required, and candidate is a complete typed all, none, some, or some-not proposition.
The question operation is either select-entailed-candidate or select-sufficient-premise.
No source sentence or candidate is ignored during projection.
Candidate identifiers carry join identity only and do not affect entailment.
invariants: Candidate permutation cannot change the selected semantic candidate.
Premise ordering cannot change satisfiability or entailment.
Complete renaming of terms and candidate identifiers preserves the structural result.
A candidate qualifies only when adding the negated query makes the monadic constraint system inconsistent.
uncertaintySemantics: Zero or several qualifying candidates return UNDERDETERMINED. An inconsistent base returns INCONSISTENT_CONTEXT. Unsupported language remains NO_APPLICABLE_METHOD at the adapter boundary.
proofBehavior: Every qualifying candidate includes a literal-closure conflict. Every nonqualifying candidate includes an explicit finite object-type countermodel. verifyCategoricalArgumentSelection independently checks derivation-edge licenses or evaluates every premise and the query in the returned object model.
kbMigration: None. The candidate is unregistered, changes no package schema, and is called only by the two source adapters after strict projection.
